memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Moses heard this, he was satisfied." - Lev 10:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four words end the chapter. Moses listened, and he was satisfied.

He did not insist on being right. He heard his brother's explanation and accepted it.

That is a remarkable moment. Moses had been angry. He had the authority, the law on his side, and a fresh memory of what happened when priests deviated from instructions. He could easily have pressed his point.

Instead he listened, and changed his mind.

Real spiritual maturity includes the ability to be persuaded. James writes that the wisdom that comes from heaven is first of all pure; then peace-loving, considerate, submissive (Jas 3:17) — that word means open to reason, willing to yield. Be quick to listen, slow to speak, slow to become angry (Jas 1:19).

Notice also what Moses does not do. He does not apologise elaborately or spiral into self-criticism. He simply accepts the explanation and moves on. That is healthy.

And so the chapter closes — not with punishment, but with two grieving brothers reaching understanding.

After the fire, mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I able to be persuaded when someone gives me a good reason?
2. Is there a conflict where I have insisted on being right rather than listening?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me quick to listen and willing to yield when I am wrong. Give me humility in conflict and grace toward those I disagree with. Amen.
